utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. May I remind you, sir, of the affirmation that you made at the beginning of your evidence, that still applies. Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, before we ended yesterday's session, we were talking over each other yesterday when I was asking you. Actually, could we display what has been marked as P00169, already admitted? It is tab 16 of the binders. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, may we move back into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now perhaps you could repeat what you were saying, Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions of this witness. There are tabs 17 through 19 of the binders. Because of the amount of time I took yesterday, I do not wish to go into these particular exhibits. You will see that they are already admitted. I do have one additional request and that is I believe we have fixed the exhibit that had been marked for identification as 252. It is now 65 ter 202.1. It was the photograph, Your Honours, that the redaction was requested of. We went ahead and actually took the photograph and made it a separate exhibit, so I would like to now admit that under -- tender that, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The photograph will now be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. M-053. I am Edina Residovic and together with my co-counsel I'm appearing for Mr. Ljube Boskoski. Before I go on to the questions, Mr. M-053, I would like to warn you on one thing. I assume that you understand the language that I speak, and I understand the language that you speak. But my question as well as your answers should be interpreted so that His Honours and the colleagues in the courtroom would be able to know what we are talking about. I would therefore like to ask you to wait a while, while my question is interpreted and then respond to it. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask Your Honours to move into a private session for a while?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The task of issuance of weapons in the police stations and in the departments of the police stations are performed in accordance with the guidelines of issuance of weapons. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to say that to perform these regular tasks that are regulated by the laws and the guidebooks, you did not need special orders, but for certain tasks you received orders from your superior officer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That orders of the immediate superior could -- could be oral or written. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are more oral.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Verbal.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And those orders could be given to you by the head of OVR Cair or a person that would be authorised by him, then the head of the defensive preparations and other authorised officials in accordance with the rules. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-053, yesterday on several occasions you responded to the questions when you were asked about some of the tasks of the Ministry of Interior. In order to make some things clearer I would like to ask you to tell me, would it be correct that in accordance to the law, the Ministry of Interior in fact represents the entire structure of all the organs of the interior, and that includes the police officers, the police stations as well as the departments of the interior in the municipalities as well as the sectors of the interior in the cities, so the entire public and state security. Is all these put together the thing that makes the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. M-053, when sometimes it -- a jargon is used to say MVR, the people only have in mind the building of the ministry on a state level in which the building in which the minister is seated, or to put it simply, if I were to say to the taxi driver in Skopje, I would like to go to the MVR, then he would took me to the building where the minister sits. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a police officer, you're aware that actually most of the tasks of the police are carried out in accordance with the law and that is in the organs that by the law or by the rules are charged to carry out certain tasks and duties. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And to make it even more simple, so the police station is responsible for the public order and peace on its territory, the commander of the police station is responsible for the situation in his police station for the safety of the people that are entering the police station and et cetera. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The department of the interior in which you used to work in Cair under its composition had the police stations Cair and Mirkovci, then there was this operational department where the inspectors or the authorised officials worked who worked on detection of crimes, then in the department of the interior there was an analysis section, and also there was an authorised official in charge of the defensive preparations. Is this roughly the structure of your department of the interior?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind that you said that most of the tasks you carried out in accordance to the law and the systemization of the jobs, that is to say, also with the order of your immediate superior, could I understand it as -- that in the -- in the performance of your duty you never got a direct order from the Ministry of the Interior on national and state level, nor from the minister himself. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your responses to the questions of my learned colleague about how the reservists were called, you testified about the mobilisation and the call to the reserve force that was coming from the minister or from persons authorised by the Minister. I'd like to ask you to clarify these facts a little bit. Is it correct, Mr. M-053, that the citizens of the Republic of Macedonia with full age after serving the military service, they are then deployed in the reserve forces of whether the police or the army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In every municipality, there is a department of the Ministry of Defence where the registers of the reserve forces are kept and upon the request of a certain police organ, this department of the defence could redeploy the reserve force so that some people would be additionally assigned to the list of the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Concerning this core formalisation that you mentioned, is it correct that it is the government actually who decides on that to mobilise the police force and after that decision, it is the minister or a person authorised by him who orders to call the reserve force in the entire country or in a certain area. Is that the way that is prescribed by the law for calling, summonsing in the reserve force?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Beside this general call which is sent to all the sectors and department of the interior, all other tasks are carried out by the authorised officials in the sector of the interior or the department of the interior in accordance with the rule book for calling the reserve force. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You personally did not perform duties to call summons and register the reserve forces. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I understood you well, in the Cair department, those tasks were carried out by your colleague Ilija Sovkovski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It wasn't your duty when persons are sent to you to issue weapons and uniforms. It wasn't your duty to check whether they were really members of the reserve force of the police. That was the duty, the task of another person. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. M-053, that in addition to these individual calls for persons that were already on the list of the Ministry of Interior, the reserve force could be also called by a public call for mobilisation? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. But you would agree with me that it is possible that this is written in some law, in some rule book. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you well when you testified yesterday, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours may we move into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: With respect to this last question, Your Honour -- my apologies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. M-053, that for someone to become a reserve police officers or to be within the reserve police forces, it would be necessary for the person to be registered in the list of reserve police officers, to be deployed at a job within a given police station or other -- or be given other police work, and these persons would need to have an ID of the reserve police forces, they were salaried by the Ministry of Interior and when all these criteria were met, then they would be considered reserve police forces. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the actual issuance of weapons and uniforms would not make a person a police officer immediately. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you actually do not know whether (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, I apologise. I apologise, Your Honours. Let's move into a private session briefly to ask this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When a person becomes a reserve police officer, you answered already, they are deployed to perform tasks within a police station or to perform other police duties; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat this question again.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When a person becomes a reserve police officer, you have testified previously that person is given certain tasks, either within a police station or elsewhere in a police body.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not able to hear the interpretation at all. It's all right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it all right now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There are interruptions. I don't know hear it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you able to hear me now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You told me already that a person enrolled in the reserve forces is deployed to perform certain police tasks, either to a police station or elsewhere on police duties. So my question now is: When a person is deployed at a police station, is it correct that, then, the responsibility for that person is assumed by the commander of the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the police station issues orders based on the deployment of the reserve forces, and they are assigning the forces with specific tasks and responsibilities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, Your Honour. I wish to look at some documents, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if that person, regardless of whether they are an active or a reserve police officer, does something in breach of the standards of performing the police works, then the responsibility falls on the commander of the police station to investigate the responsibility of that person. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned colleague showed you yesterday and today a number of documents, so I ask you now to look at them again. It is P170. That is the report about the use of means of enforcement of fire-arms. Do you see now at the top of this page, it reads: Ministry of Interior, then office of internal affairs, Cair, department for internal affairs, Cair, police station, Cair. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that document, if we look at the next page of it, was signed by the authorised officer of that police station, Ziljanov Tome, who is a corporal -- INTERPRETER: Sergeant, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask that the witness is shown the Exhibit P174 again. That is a statement of a person. And is it correct that in the top section of this document it again reads Ministry of Internal Affairs, police station Cair. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And again the document is signed by an authorised officer of that police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were also shown the document P175.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I'd like to ask that it is shown again.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is one more statement, and again, in the top section you see that it is written that it was the Ministry of Interior, police station Cair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then this statement is signed by the authorised officer of that police station; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now I would like to ask you to look at P170, P169, which was also shown to you. Do you see that this report about a procedure conducted at a police station was forwarded to the sector for internal affairs, Skopje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to these documents, I wish to ask you: Is it correct that with regards to the responsibility of the police station commander for the acts of his or her subordinate officers, it is actually the police station, the body that has the duty to instigate a procedure, if they have any information that their officer, that a police officer or a person from within that police station has done something outside of the professional standards for the conduct of police officers, would that be the duty of that police station and of that police station commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the overall procedure, as we have seen here, end with a report sent to the sector for security in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is written on the second page to whom is the report sent.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It reads here that -- so apart from the fact that is written to the SVR Skopje, as it is written on the first page, in the second page, later as you properly -- as you rightly stated, it says that it was also forwarded to the unit, then to the analytics department in Cair and a copy remained in the police station. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Otherwise, could you agree with me that disciplinary procedures against any officer of the Ministry of Interior are conducted pursuant to the collective agreement, which precisely stipulates the procedures and the bodies deciding on the responsibility or liability of an officer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We would now move to another line of questions which are not related the procedure that you discussed with my learned colleague, the Prosecutor. Is it correct that in 2001 many people were enrolled in the police -- in the reserve forces in the Cair department?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to say that for 50 active police officers, and that was the number of you before the time of the crisis, in that year there were some 300 to 350 reserve police officers enrolled, that would be the approximate number of police officers in your department. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the situation that existed as well as the big number of newly enrolled persons actually prevented the full control over the entire forces from existing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stated already that there were two police stations within the realms of the department Cair. They were the stations Cair and Mirkovci?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that after the Ljuboten events, a reserve police station was established on the 15th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was warned that the interpreting is possibly insufficiently precise. But I think we will go back to it later, because the question and the answer were recorded on page 21, line 21 to 24.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the reserve police station was established after the events in Ljuboten, on the 15th of August 2001; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This police station covered also the village of Ljuboten, but the police officers were not able to enter the village all the way until the start of 2002; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you actually aware that it is only the mixed police patrols with the assistance of OSCE and NATO and the Amber Fox, the ones who entered the village at the beginning of 2002?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 2nd or the 3rd of January, 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And up until then actually the police officers from the Cair department were unable to perform any police duties in the village of Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But because you worked at that department for a number of years after that, could you then testify that even after that time the Ljuboten villagers, the Albanians, were not prepared and willing to cooperate with the Macedonian police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that time that you testified about, the security situation in your municipality had deteriorated significantly because of the fact that in the area of the municipality pertained also part of the Skopska Crna Gora, which, due to its closeness to the Kumanovo crisis area and to the Kosovo border, was of special significance to the security of Skopje as well. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. M-053, was this the reason for the army of the Republic of Macedonia to expand its control over the border area, that is the border towards Serbia and Kosovo, by deploying its units also in part of the area of the municipality of Cair near the Ljuboten village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the putting of mines by Albanian terrorists in the Ljubotenski Bacila when eight members of the Macedonian army were killed and some of them were wounded has additionally deteriorated the situation in your municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You must be aware that two of the killed members of the army were from the Ljubanci village, which was also under the competences of the municipality of Cair; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood well, when you answered to the questions of my learned colleague, on the 10th of -- the people of Ljubanci village, as of the 10th have started to come and request weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The closeness of these terrorist attacks has provoked fear among the people, and there were information that part of the terrorists had entered the village. Were you aware of such information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew something and I did not know some other things.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you said, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, Your Honour, I would like this to be redacted and to go to a private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private. Redaction.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The superior organ over the OVR Cair was the department of interior of Skopje, the sector, I'm sorry, of interior in Skopje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sector of interior of Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Okay, thank you. And the direct superior to your head, the assistant of SVR Skopje, the minister assistant of SVR Skopje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The office of SVR Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And at that time this was Mr. Zoran Efremov; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you a few things related to the -- to your testimony concerning some events of August 12th. If I understood well, upon the -- upon the call of your head and upon his order on the 12th in the morning at about 10.00 you went to monitor the police check-points; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have visited the Ljubance check-point as well; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ljubanci, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During that visit at around 1.00 p.m., the head Krstevski was informed that Minister Boskoski was coming; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He told you then to go to the playfield which was -- which is located on the road to Ljubanci and to meet the minister; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When the minister arrived, you could see immediately that he was accompanied by some TV reporters, some journalists; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The minister greeted with your head and with all of you that met him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were here nearby when he greeted with your head?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I would say to you that the minister at that time asked your head what was happening and that your head briefly explained the situation, you would agree with me that this was the right description of the events; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said you didn't enter the Brace's house and that you stayed by the gate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that not far from that gate there were people that were brought in, that were lying there by the wall. These persons were brought in from the Ljuboten village by the people that were in the village of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: To the question of my learned colleague you said that these were civilians. In that respect, I would like to ask you the following: As a police officer and as a citizen who could see the reports from the events in the crisis areas, could you see on the TV that the members of the NLA in the past sometimes wore uniforms while some other times wore some combined uniforms, partly civilian and partially military uniforms, and that sometimes in the reports you could see members of the NLA with arms wearing only civilian clothes. Could you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In these reports you could even see sometimes children with weapons; is that correct? Have you ever seen such things?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. These people that were brought to the Brace house by people with masks, if I would say that those people who brought them in said that they had captured them in fight, would this be correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat this question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I asked whether the people who brought in the people from Ljuboten, these are the people that you described when answering to the question of my learned colleague, people wearing masks, did these people at the time when they brought in the other people who said that they had captured them in combat in the village of Ljuboten, or maybe you are not aware of the way these people have been captured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, if I say at the moment you saw these people and the weapons that were brought from the village that you were convinced these were people who had participated in combat, then you could agree now that this was so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could please you repeat this question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So I'll put it in a simpler way. At the moment when you saw these people and when you saw the weapons that were brought from the village, is it true that at that point, at that moment, you considered that these people were people who had been captured in combat? Is this the way you thought at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the witness to be displayed Exhibit P -- this was 65 ter 566, but I think yesterday it was given number D -- P262.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned colleague yesterday showed you this document, and she said that this was -- this was operative information, and you corrected her and said that this was an Official Note. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you to look at the second line where it writes: Detainment of arrested individuals. Namely, I would like to ask you whether somewhere here you see whether the word "arrested" is written?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see "brought in."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But do you see "arrested?" You do not see any word which points to the fact that these are arrested people. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this respect I would ask you the following: As a police officer, you know that the police forces can bring in a certain individual in the police station and hold him up to 24 hours. This is in accordance with the law of the Republic of Macedonia. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The police cannot -- not detain a person unless there is a decision from an investigating judge; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After 24 hours, each -- every person that is brought in must be released unless the investigating judge has given an agreement of -- for-- for him to be held or to -- to be detained. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you look at this note, and this detention is decided upon the public prosecutions [as interpreted]. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you to see the fourth paragraph in this note. You can see that the proposal to hold these individuals -- I apologise, in paragraph 2, you could see that the deputy public prosecutor Lazar Natrandziski, together with deputy Jovo Serafimovski, have reached the given agreement. This is written in paragraph 2. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then, in paragraph 4 it writes that upon -- that the investigating judge of the lower court Skopje II, Bekir Sani, was informed of this recommendation by the above-mentioned deputy of the court of first instance and the head -- and the end, it was agreed -- it was said that they had reached a joint agreement confirmed by the investigating judge of the Lower court Skopje II, Bekir Sani, and that these persons were held until the end of the overall procedure. This was -- but you agree that this was the only way to keep certain individuals in the police station over 24 hours because the investigating judge had decided that. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if we look at the name of the investigating judge, Bekir Sani, you would agree that this is an investigating judge of Albanian ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, I have completed with the questioning of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Residovic. Given the hour, I think probably if we had the break, the first break now, it would give Mr. Apostolski time to be ready to commence when we resume at five minutes to 11.00. So we will adjourn now for the first break and resume at five to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness M-053, I'm Antonio Apostolski and I'm the main counsel of Mr. Johan Tarculovski, together with my colleague, Jasmina Zivkovic. She is the co-counsel in this case. I will ask you some questions regarding the events between 10th and 12th August, 2001. May we begin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: If we could go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: On 10th of August, 2001, a Friday, in the vicinity of Ljuboten village, eight soldiers were killed and eight others injuries due to the mine that was laid there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is this -- is it correct that this act was carried out by the NLA terrorist group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that on the 18th of August, 2001, in a similar ambush, members of the Macedonian security forces were killed at Karpalak location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I apologise, I mean 8th of August.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 8th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that this act was also carried out by the members of the NLA terrorist group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: A similar ambush occurred at Vejce, in the month of May, whereby the survivors from the Macedonian security forces ranks were massacred. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it also correct that this attack was also carried out by the NLA terrorist group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that following these actions, the NLA members would withdraw to settlements or areas inhabited by ethnic Albanians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that in your police station you had information that part of the group that carried out the attack in the vicinity of Ljuboten village on the 10th of August, 2001, in which Macedonian soldiers were killed, withdrew in Ljuboten village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Ljuboten village was a logistics base of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I will now ask you some questions in relation to Sunday, 12th August 2001. On this Sunday, at around 9.00, you went to work, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: There you heard that there was shooting in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: At around 11.00, you went to tour the check-points in the vicinity of Ljubanci and Ljuboten villages, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: At around 11.30, you arrived at the Chinese wall check-point, right? Around 11.30, I would say.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Earlier, around 11.00, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: All right. When you arrived at Chinese wall check-point, from the direction of Ljuboten, there was automatic and sniper fire coming and directed at you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The fire came from three or four houses located on a hill in Ljuboten village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Through binoculars, you saw smoke coming from fire-arms, from the windows of these houses, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like now to show the witness a photograph, N005-7603. This is a panoramic photograph of Ljuboten village.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is a panoramic photograph of Ljuboten village as depicted from the side of Radisani. Could you please show me on this photograph --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The check-point, our check-point is somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: On this side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Brace house on the right side, you cannot see the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you -- we could move the photograph to the right a little bit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: If we could move the photograph to the right. Please wait for a while. The usher will move the photograph so that you can see it better. With the assistance of the usher, could you please mark or circle that location. If you need to, we can enlarge the photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we could enlarge the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can enlarge it on the right-hand side. A little bit more, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see now those houses on the photograph, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here is the Brace house, somewhere here. It should be here somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: We enlarged the photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It is opposite the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is the right-hand side of the village. Can you mark with number 1 the houses from where you saw --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are three houses up there, 1, 2, 3, here are the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you mark with number 1 the houses from where you saw smoke coming out from fire-arms, from the windows of the houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These houses are opposite to our check-point, immediately to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this photograph as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit 2D26, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: A group of ten persons that were brought in -- a group of ten persons were brought in, in front of Brace's house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: From the persons who brought them in, you found out that these persons, before they were brought in, were wearing uniforms and later on they changed their clothes and put on civilian clothes. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that one of NLA's tactics was for its members to change into civilian clothes and mingle with the local population?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Afterwards, you returned to the Cair police station, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You noticed that there were persons who were brought in in this police station, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You did not see or notice any one of them being beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Most of them were brought in in the police station, right? Held in the police station, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that only those persons who get a positive paraffin glove test were -- were held in the police station and brought before the court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Those persons whose results were negative were released and allowed to go home, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski. Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, you were asked, and I believe the reference is on page 7 of today's transcript. You were asked about the tasks of police. On the 12th of August, 2001, do you know what the tasks of the police were? And to clarify, this is in relation to the police that you saw at Brace's house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were deployed on the check-points for security reasons.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And on page 8 of today's transcript you were asked about not getting direct orders from the Minister of Interior. In 2001 if you had received a direct order from the Minister of Interior, would you have followed it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This has to arrive first at the senior officer who is appointed in the police station, and then he issued that order to me to carry it out.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, he relays that order to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And later on page 18 of today's transcript you stated that it is the commander of the police station who is responsible for investigating breaches of duty by police officers. What if the commander of the police station does not investigate a particular breach? Who is then responsible for the investigation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is internal control.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And what do you mean by "internal control"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a department of internal control that investigates these cases when a senior officer fails to undertake the necessary measures against his employees.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And later on page 21 of today's transcript, you spoke about a number of reservists in 2001. Were the reservists deployed from OVR Cair in 2001 under the authority of a superior officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Can I just go back to a question that I asked you earlier with respect to an order, a direct order from the Minister of Interior. My question was if you had received a direct order from the Minister of Interio , would have you follow it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the witness answered this question, and it is a question of an order for mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I must say I have a concern, Ms. Motoike, but it is perhaps directed to a different point. That is, this is entirely conjectural, because it is the evidence of this witness that there was never any direct order ever received by him ever in the course of his employment. Would you like to put submissions dealing both with Ms. Residovic's point and with mine?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I guess my -- I understand what the witness testified to, Your Honour. With respect, though, to his position as a police officer in the department, my question was only asking whether or not as a Minister of Interior if he had received an order, hypothetically speaking, because he is a still a police officer, was a police officer at that time, in 2001, if he had received an order, would it then be his obligation to follow it through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is a question different from the one that you did ask, because you're asking whether there was an obligation to obey, not what this person would do. Now, there is the other submission of Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. Could I have just a moment. With respect to my learned colleague's submission, I don't believe -- perhaps the way I phrased question, the answer might have been already given. But I would like an opportunity, with the Court's leave, to rephrase the question specifically geared to what I was asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That, I think will deal both with my concern and the point of Ms. Residovic's observation. I think her objection was directed to the way you had formulated your question, which certainly seemed to be something you had certainly dealt with earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Witness, if you had -- as a police officer at the Cair police station, if you had received an order from the Minister of the Interior would it had been your duty as a police officer to follow that order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not me who will receive the order directly. It is the senior officer who receives this order and then he relays that order to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And on page 35 of today's transcript, you were asked -- or actually, you indicated that Ljuboten was a logistics base of the NLA. Was this based on information from -- that you had within your police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, were all the persons who resided in Ljuboten village members of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And you were also asked on page 38 of today's transcripts, you were -- actually indicated that you had been informed that some of these persons that had been brought in had uniforms on at one time. Did you see any of those uniforms that these persons had referred to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see uniforms, but I knew that they had changed their clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And that knowledge was based on other persons who had informed you at the scene?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M-053 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, may we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just repeat for the public record that your questioning has concluded, and the Chamber thanks you for your attendance and the evidence you have given, and you may now go with the court officer. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next witness will be led by Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And is this a witness with protective measures, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I believe not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Not. And this witness's name, Mr. Neuner?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Ali Isni. Mr. Isni Ali.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, apparently it is difficult to locate the witness. May I have the Chamber's leave to call a member of the Prosecution team who may know the specific room where the witness is waiting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Ali. Would you please read the affirmation that is on the card.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I solemnly declare to say the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down. Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Ali.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner has some questions for you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Ali. Your name is Isni Ali?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And your -- I don't receive a translation.

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do Your Honours receive a translation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your ethnicity is Albanian?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you live in the village of Ljuboten in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in October 2003, you provided a first statement to the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in September 2004 you gave a second statement to the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in November 2005, you met in Ljuboten a representative from the registry who certified the first statement you gave in October 2003?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in April of this year, you met my colleague and myself in Ljuboten and made corrections and additions to your first statement from 2003?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And did you have the opportunity to read these documents before you came here today?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And are you satisfied that the contents are accurate?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, according to Rule 92 bis I'd like to tender the certified first statement of this witness into evidence. The ERN number is N002-1694 to 1703.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P263, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I also wish to tender the statement from April this year containing the additions and corrections to this 92 bis statement into evidence. ERN is N006-4323 to 4331.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, very briefly. We had understood that the Prosecution would only seek to tender the actual statements of -- or addendum, I should say, of Mr. Ali, which would be the first three pages of the addendum. But not the comments, if I may say so, which come thereafter, which are essentially comments made by the witness in relation to certain exhibits. We had made submissions earlier in the day in relation to another witness, Your Honour, to the effect that we understood that if the Prosecution intends to lead particular evidence in relation to an exhibit, they could do that at the time of tendering the statement and would then lead the evidence from the witness in relation to these exhibits. We understand from the information which we received yesterday from the Prosecution that they do not intend to seek to tender some of the exhibits which are mentioned in this addendum. To that extent, it is our submission that the Prosecution would not or should not be permitted to tender these comments of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I will clarify very briefly, taking the comments of my colleague on board. I will therefore seek only the first three pages as suggested by my learned friend into evidence and I will read it in the record. The ERN number is N006-4323 to N006-4325.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You realise the Chamber does not have these supplementary materials. We received the filing of the original statement with the 92 bis submission. We do not get any of these additions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would have a hard copy available, which, if Your Honours so wish, could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it is a matter to see what it is that you want to tender following Mr. Mettraux's point and concerns.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yeah. So if it could be please placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think if it is just shown to us at the moment. Counsel already have it, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, it may involve some extra time, but it appears to the Chamber that the original statement which you tender is the statement that is authorised pursuant to Rule 92 bis. This addendum is not a statement within either 92 bis or ter, and if it is, there are passages in the original 92 bis statement that the witness now seeks to explain or vary in some particular, then that should be done orally rather than by attempting to tender the addendum, which is really a form of notice to the Defence so that they are prepared for these changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We are prepared to follow that proposed course of action, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Neuner. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That solve the issue, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The original statement will be received pursuant to Rule 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The date of the 92 bis statement, Mr. Neuner, is? October 2003?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It is the 29th of October, 2003 and my understanding from the first two cover pages, meaning the registry's cover pages that, the registry officer, Ms. Katarina Fabian has on the 18th of November, 2005, approached this witness with an Albanian translation of that 2003 statement and asked him to read through -- or it was read out to him then and certified in that moment. If this assists Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, the statement you're tendering pursuant to 92 bis is that dated in April -- in October of 2003?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It says 29th of October, 2003, on page with the ERN N002-1696.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you also tendering the Albanian translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is indeed the Albanian -- or the -- the Albanian version as certified on the 18th of November, 2005, by the registry officer in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And attached to that are English translations as well as Macedonian translations. They should be attached in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now are you wishing to deal with these other issues?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, I will. May I first have an opportunity to summarize what is in this statement just tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The witness Isni Ali a Ljuboten resident of Albanian ethnicity. On 10 to 12 August, 2001, Macedonian forces launched an attack against Ljuboten. The witness's son Erxhan was killed by a grenade during the attack on Friday, 10 August 2001. On Sunday, 12 August 2001, at 10.00 in the morning, the grenade hit the witness's house. On 12th of August, 2001, the witness and other villagers fled Ljuboten. On his way, he saw the body of Sulejman Bajrami near the Ametovski house. The witness arrived at the Buzalak check-point where he saw police and a number of detained men who appear to have been beaten. The witness and others were taken to Prolece police station. There the witness was beaten so severely by police officers that he lost consciousness. Later he under went a paraffin test at Prolece police station. The witness and other detainees were mistreated and beaten there. On the second night, the witness and others were transferred to Bit Pazar police station. He was beaten and detained there for 24 hours. The witness was then taken to Skopje Court where policemen beat him and others on the corridor. In court, the witness was forced to sign a statement. He was imprisoned in Sutka prison for about four month, after which he was released. The witness still suffers from pain in his kidneys and cannot sleep on his right side because of the injuries he suffered during the mistreatment in August 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Ali, I want to take you to Prolece police station you were taken there on Sunday, the 12th of August, 2001. In paragraph 9 of your statement you mentioned that you were seriously beaten there?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And at some point in time, you were taken into an office to undertake a test.

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please describe what happened when you were entering the office door.

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: When we entered the door of the paraffin test room, they opened the door, they pushed us from behind, and they closed the door. And we hit the door with our heads. Then they put our heads under the table. They put our hands on the table. Then they hit us with Kalashnikov butts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I just stop you here.

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: We -- we felt something like rubber or plastic. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I stop you for a second, please. What did you see -- what persons did you see in the room?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: We saw the police officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what did they have in their hands, if anything?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: They had weapons, Kalashnikovs, knives.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So can you continue, you were putting your hands on the table. And what happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note that the witness might be on the Macedonian channel because he tends to start his answers in Macedonian and then proceeds in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... put our hands on the table, they hit our hands with the Kalashnikov butts. They maltreated us there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I just stop for a second. I got an interpreter's note that the usher may please check the channel of the witness, whether the witness is receiving Albanian translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hear in Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can we change the channel to the Albanian channel, please? Are you now receiving a translation in your language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to take this step by step. So you stated that your head was put below the table; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And your hands were put above the table?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: After that, they hit with us the Kalashnikov butts. They put some kind of plastic or rubber, I don't exactly know what it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And how long did the test last?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: This test lasted for about ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you said: They hit with us Kalashnikov butts. What part of your body was hit?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: They hit us on our hands and on our back.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what happened after the test was over?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: After the test was over, they took us to another room and they continued beating us in all possible ways.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You state in your statement that you stayed at Prolece police station until Monday evening, the 13th of August, 2001. My question to is: During the entire stay you had at Prolece police station, were you ever interviewed?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Were you ever asked any questions about events in Ljuboten on the 10th to 12th August 2001 at Prolece police station?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, I would like to hand out some exhibits. We have enough copies also for the Defence. I would like to ask the usher to use tab 5 first with the witness. You had enough copies. I gave you ... The admitted exhibit number is P51, ERN number is N002-0082. An Official Note from 13th August 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In its first paragraph the document mentions nine persons and your name, Mr. Ali, is also mentioned there. Do you find your name?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It states in that first paragraph that on the 12th of August, in the police station Kisela Voda interviews were conducted. My question to you is: Were you, as it is alleged in that document here, interviewed at the police station, Kisela Voda, or Prolece that night?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I can go on to the third paragraph of that document, it states, talking about the nine persons, including you, that with regard to the events in Ljuboten, the following occurred there, and I quote now: "The persons allegedly said," and I quote, "'shooting could be heard at each side of the village. Actually, fire was led between the police of the Republic of Macedonia and the terrorist gangs. The above-mentioned persons stated they noticed many terrorists engaged in fights having weapons.'"? Do you recall that you --

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... this information?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you could please look at tab 4 in the binder in front of you. ERN is N004-4887. What do you recognise on this picture?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: This is the Bit Pazar police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And had you been -- what happened on that weekend or after that weekend, in relation to Bit Pazar police station?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: They took us to the basement in some basement cells. They maltreated us very much and there was a police officer there I knew named Goran. There were other police officers as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to tender that document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P264, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In the statement you stated that in the evening of 14th of August you were taken out of that police station, Bit Pazar, to be transferred to the Skopje Court. What happened to you when you were boarding the van?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Here again, we were ill-treated. My nose was broken. They took us in the van, and from there, they took us to the court. In the Court, they also maltreated us. In the hall, they beat us. There was a -- a judge there who walked on my -- on my feet and she told the police, "Why did you bring them here? Why didn't you kill them?" From there we entered the court.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I just ask you who was beating you in the hall of the Skopje Court?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: The police, and there was a female judge who walked on my legs and she wanted to cut off my toes. I was wearing sandals.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Why do you believe it was the police who beat you?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Because they were wearing uniforms and they had weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What type of uniform?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Police --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you describe --

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: -- uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you describe the colour or the insignia?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Yes. They had police insignia. They had also on their arms the insignia of their grades.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what colour did the uniforms have?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Blue, police colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And since there's also possibility that it could be the court police, do you remember that this is --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to object. I really apologise, but this is enormously leading, and my colleague knows that this is very much a live issue in the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, what type of policemen were beating you in the Skopje hall -- in the hall of the Skopje Court?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: There were police officers, reservists, and active police officers who were on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When you, after the beating, had to enter the courtroom, how did you look?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Then we were 90 per cent exhausted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And how was your face looking like?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Face was covered with blood and my nose was broken.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what happened inside the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: In the courtroom, we were seated. We were read all the documents. I only -- I was given a paper to sign. They said, "Either you sign or I will call the police in the courtroom." And this is what I did. I signed the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You say "they said." Who spoke these words to you?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: There were members of the court, there was a lawyer and there was a person writing on a writing machine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And who of these persons spoke these words to you?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: The judge, and if I see this judge, I can recognise him or her.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, it is 12.30. If you wish to go for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is time for the second break, Mr. Neuner, if that is convenient. And we will resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Ali, I want to take you to tab 6 of your binder, and the document in tab 6. Exhibit number is P55, 65 ter number 21.27, ERN number N002-1220 to 1221.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to ask you a question, because there are two mistakes made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. What is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The name of my son is recorded as "Erhan." His name is Erxhan. And it had has been recorded that he was killed on the 12th, but he was killed on the 10th of August, in the afternoon, on that Friday. And I was not taken in at Buzalak. I was taken in at the location called Kodra e Zajmit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. That seems to be three matters that you identified that you feel are not correct in this. The spelling of your son, when he was killed, and where you were taken in.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Does that help you, Mr. Neuner?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Ali, if you could please look at page 2 of that document. I believe it is the first line in the Macedonian translation, or in the Macedonian original. Is here your son's name spelled correctly, Erxhan?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Yes, here it is correctly, Erxhan.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in the middle -- in the lower middle of that page, do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: This is written in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry. The witness might look at the English translation and not at the original. ERN is N002-1221 of that page. It is tab 6, I believe. My question was: Do you recognise the signature in the lower middle of the page?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: One of them I do, but not the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Which one do you recognise?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: The first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In the middle of the page?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Whose signature is this, please?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I have read this document and my understanding is this is a statement you gave. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I don't understand the document to be a statement, Your Honour. Those are notes taken of an interview or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for interrupting you, but this is not my signature and this is not my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So since you signed that document, can you explain what your understanding was at the time you signed it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: He's just said it is not his signature, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay, sorry. Then I was confused, because on page 66 the witness said it was my signature. Page 66, line 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can we clarify this. The middle signature on that page, because I asked that earlier, is that your signature or is it not your signature, as you said a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: I'm not sure about this signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I take you back to the first page of that document, please. On the upper part of that document, does it state your name here?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And I read here the date, 21st of March, 2002.

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you recall maybe an event on that day?

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: 21st of March 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It says in my translation 2002 and in the original as well.

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you're right, 2002. 21st of March, 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I may put you to the second page of that document, back again.

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The last paragraph talks about a hearing and the persons being present there.

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Now I understood your question. That's correct. It is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In the lower middle -- in the lower middle part of the document.

utterances.speaker: ISNI ALI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
